review_scope: Fresh-context review of K3 only, after AGENTS.md, README introduction, and PROJECT_STATE stage/objective/optimization_contracts. No other proof or reviewer report consulted.

comprehension.own_words: A finite dependency-complete DAG of total deterministic value computations has schedule-independent values. An intact cache entry can replace a node when key equality guarantees equality of its complete observable result. An approximate entry instead has a local deterministic error at most eta + L*d, provided both inputs lie in the certified Lipschitz region and eta bounds the stored representative error.
derivation_checks: Longest-predecessor-path induction is valid for every node of a finite DAG, including disconnected components and shared predecessors; ordered inputs preserve noncommutative argument roles. It establishes values, not execution cost or infinite-stream behavior.

The cache implication is quantified over all admitted colliding keys, not merely observed hits. Completed evaluation, retained value, and lookup-time sufficiency give substitution equality; induction allows arbitrary finite combinations of valid hits.

The approximate-key inequality is exactly the triangle inequality followed by the assumed pairwise Lipschitz bound. Convexity or differentiability of the bucket is unnecessary when Lipschitz continuity itself is assumed; neither a checked center nor isolated sample derivatives would establish that premise.
counterexample_attempts: Two otherwise independent nodes accessing mutable state can change results when reordered. This violates the explicit versioned-state/effect-dependency premises, so it is an implementation failure rather than a counterexample.

A stale pointer key, wrapped generation, hash collision, or torn key/value read can return a wrong result. The proof expressly excludes each through sufficiency, full-key/collision requirements, retained values, and atomic generation premises.

Treating +0 and -0 as interchangeable numeric values can change a downstream reciprocal to opposite signed infinities. Observable value equality must therefore be preserved by every downstream consumer. The signed-zero and numerical-equality caveat already identifies this boundary; a declaration of coarse equality alone cannot establish the premise.

A discontinuous authorization/status output at a bucket boundary need not admit a finite Lipschitz bound. Such a bucket is outside the approximate theorem unless the output is handled by an exact guard or separately justified comparison.

For f(x)=abs(x), the value is 1-Lipschitz, but derivatives at +/-epsilon differ by 2 while the value bound is 2*epsilon. The value theorem cannot be reused as a derivative bound; the instruction to propagate defects including derivative outputs must be discharged for the actual derivative-producing map.

Repeated reuse of one biased cache value, or a downstream gain A, can produce cumulative error or amplification. The theorem claims only a per-use local defect and explicitly requires propagation; it supplies no independent-noise or global-error guarantee.

Skipping source consumption, floating-point flags, failure reporting, or a deadline-related effect can change full-machine behavior despite equal numerical values. These are expressly excluded from the pure result and assigned separate transition/refinement obligations.

remaining_application_obligations: Specify the admitted domain and complete observable result semantics. Equality must be a congruence for all graph consumers; exact representation equality suffices when bitwise outputs are claimed. Account for signed zeros, NaNs, rounding modes, and exception behavior.

Construct a finite single-assignment graph with fixed external inputs, immutable configuration, and complete dependencies for physical state, chronology, ownership, and all serialized effects. Establish determinism and totality on the admitted domain.

Prove cache-key sufficiency for every admitted lookup, including all kernel/configuration/dependency versions; prove retained entry integrity, completed-value publication, generation consistency, and collision/wrap handling.

Implement and verify once-only effect behavior for source consumption, counters, error/status reporting, floating-point flags, and other declared observables. Establish full-machine fault/timing refinement separately.
Choose input/output norms and certify L, d, eta and bucket membership on the entire admitted bucket. Include all changing numerical dependencies and match or bound every discrete change.

If values, Jacobians, gradients, uncertainty, or state transports are cached together, bound the actual joint output map or provide distinct justified component bounds. A value Lipschitz constant alone does not bound derivatives.

Propagate each deterministic cache-use defect through downstream computation and repeated invocations, preserving correlations and decision margins. No global lifetime bound, measurement-noise model, or physical codebook restriction follows from K3.

Establish registry/storage lifetimes, worst-case memory and execution time, invalidation latency, guard costs, and fault behavior for the concrete implementation. This acceptance certifies only the conditional mathematics.
